title: ESKER PLEADS NOT GUILTY
full_story:
An Effingham County man plead not guilty and is requesting a jury trial in a case in which he is facing charges related to the predatory sexual assault of a child.

In court on Wednesday, 34-year-old Jeffrey R. Esker of Teutopolis appeared and waived his formal arraignment.  He also entered a “not guilty” plea for the two counts of predatory criminal sexual assault involving a victim under the age of 13.

A pretrial hearing was set for May 6th, and Esker was remanded back to the custody of the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office ahead of the trial.

According to the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office an Effingham County Grand Jury indicted Esker on six additional felony counts of aggravated criminal sexual abuse, which are Class 2 felonies.

These indictments came as the result of an investigation by the Sheriff’s Office that began on December 2nd.  In the initial case, an arrest warrant was issued and served on Esker for two counts of predatory criminal sexual assault involving a victim under the age of 13, which are Class X felonies.

During their continued investigation, the Sheriff’s Office said Effingham County detectives identified additional victims, which led to the additional charges.

At this time, Esker remains in custody at the Effingham County Jail.

title: REDUCED RATE LABS
full_story:
Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics will be hosting their popular “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” beginning April 15th through April 30th.  You may at any time pick up a voucher at the Clay County Hospital, or at the Flora, Louisville or Clay City Clinics during regular business hours.

The blood draws must be completed April 15th through April 30th.  The hours for the blood draws are Monday – Friday, 7 am – 7 pm and Saturdays from 7 am -11 am at the Clay County Hospital.  Please complete your voucher before registering.  Payment is due at registration.

Regular blood tests are an essential part of your preventative health care plan.  Multiple choices of labs are available for you to select on the voucher. The popular “Lab Fair Panel” results include the kidney and liver functions, complete blood count, and measure cholesterol levels and triglycerides.  Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics thanks you for choosing them as your choice of healthcare and they look forward to serving you during the “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” April 15th through April 30th.

title: NO BODY TO MURDER
full_story:
A play titled “No Body to Murder” will be held at Nostalgia Theater, formerly the Town Theater, in downtown Flora.  The play will be held on Friday, April 10th, and Saturday, April 11th, at 7 pm each night.  This fun whodunnit takes place on a stormy night and will have you laughing along and keep you guessing.  This is a stage performance, not a murder mystery event and there will be no audience participation.

The play is directed by Stacey Earleywine and is full of amazing local talent, who will blow you away with their acting abilities.  Although this play is not a musical, it is full of great songs in between scenes.

Grab a friend and enjoy an evening out with well-known community theater members Jeremy Kohn, Jim Earleywine, Matt Lovett, Jessica Muskopf, Linda Waller, Sarah Hager, and more.

Nostalgia Theater is currently being renovated and will serve as Clay County’s home for community theater.  Not only will you be able to catch some amazing live entertainment at Nostalgia, but the building is also for rent as a venue for upcoming events, such as parties, reunions, showers, and weddings.

Nostalgia Theater operates as a 501©3 non-profit and all proceeds from the Nostalgia play performances will be used to continue the renovation of the theater.  Make plans to attend this fun performance, support the hard work these actors have put into it, and see the beautiful Nostalgia Theater building as it is being brought back to life.

Tickets are $10 each.  Tickets are on sale Wednesday through Friday at Cuttin’ Up Hair Salon, next to Nostalgia Theater.  Tickets will also be available at the door.

title: ROADSIDE SAFETY CHECKS
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) Troop 9 Commander, Lieutenant Bruce Waggoner, announced that the ISP will conduct Roadside Safety Checks in Effingham County during April.  The use of Roadside Safety Checks combine a strong sense of public awareness and enforcement in order to save lives of the motoring public.

The ISP has zero tolerance for impaired driving in Illinois.  Officers working the detail will be watchful for motorists who show signs of impaired driving, operating vehicles in an unsafe manner, driving with a suspended or revoked driver’s license, and transporting open alcoholic beverages, as well as improper seatbelt and child restraint usage, distracted driving, and other Illinois Vehicle Code violations.

Alcohol and drug impairment are estimated to be a factor in more than 47% of all fatal motor vehicle crashes in Illinois.  There is one alcohol-related traffic fatality every 39 minutes in the United States.  Roadside Safety Checks are designed to keep our roads safe by taking dangerous DUI offenders off the road.

This project is funded through the Illinois Department of Transportation.

title: HOME SCHOOL PARENTS
full_story:
It was home school parents who made the trip to Springfield Thursday to talk with lawmakers about their children and homeschool efforts.

It was the second year in a row that homeschool parents traveled from all parts of the state, causing State Representative Blaine Whilhour to remind his Democrat colleagues that it was last year that they woke a sleeping giant when Democrat lawmakers pushed to expand government into the homes of homeschool families and people from all over the state responded loudly.

Wilhour went on to remind the body why that effort failed.  He said “it failed because homeschool families are not really a special interest group.  They’re not lobbyists.  They’re not funded organizations.  They’re parents.  And when parents across Illinois from every part, rural, suburban, urban, when they’re all saying the same thing, maybe we ought to listen, because what you heard last year was not just opposition to a bill, it’s rejection of an attitude that’s been too pervasive here for generations.  An attitude that says government knows better than parents.  An attitude that says if something exists outside of the system, then it must be brought under control.  Here’s the reality.  The families that you tried to regulate last year, they’re succeeding.”

title: SPRING TROUT SEASON
full_story:
The 2026 Illinois spring trout fishing season will open next Saturday, April 4th at 58 ponds, lakes, and streams throughout the state.

An early opportunity at select trout sites, the spring catch-and-release fishing season, is now open.  No trout may be kept during the catch-and-release period, but anglers can keep trout after the opening of the regular season beginning April 4th.  The daily harvest limit for each angler is five trout.

Trout Fishing can be done at the Sam Dale Lake State Fish and Wildlife Area in Wayne County, at the Turkey Run Shelter Pond, because the trout pond continues to undergo rehabilitation.  Signs directing anglers to the temporary site will be posted.  At the Mount Vernon Game Farm Pond in Jefferson County, or at the Beall Woods Lake, at the Beall Woods State Park, in Wabash County, and the Boston Pond, at the Stephen A. Forbes State Recreation Area in Marion County.

For information about all site regulations, anglers should contact individual sites that will be stocked with catchable-size trout.  Not all sites are open for trout catch-and-release season and not all sites are open at 5 am opening day.

The Illinois Catchable Trout Program receives funding support by those who use the program through the sale of inland trout stamps.  The Illinois Department of Natural Resources stocks more than 80,000 rainbow trout each year in bodies of water where trout fishing is permitted during the spring season.  An additional 80,000 trout will be stocked for the fall trout season, which begins in October.

The spring trout season offers opportunities for families to get outdoors and enjoy fishing.  All anglers must have a fishing license and an inland trout stamp unless they are younger than 16, blind or disabled, or are an Illinois resident on leave from active duty in the Armed Forces.

Fishing licenses and trout stamps can be purchased by using a credit card online.  Visit ifishillinois.org for more information on trout seasons and other Illinois fishing opportunities.

title: TURKEY FEDERATION SCHOLARSHIP
full_story:
The Illinois State Chapter of the National Wild Turkey Federation is now accepting scholarship applications.  Applicants must be Illinois residents enrolled in a public community college, public four-year college, or public university in Illinois.  Eligible majors include conservation, wildlife management, ecology, conservation law enforcement, wildlife medicine, or related fields approved by the committee.

For details and how to apply, visit ilnwtf.org and click on “Scholarships.”  Application must be postmarked by Saturday, May 1st.

title: PHOTO CONTEST
full_story:
Illinois State Treasurer Michael Frerichs is calling on young Illinois photographers to submit their agriculture-related photos for the 2026 Cream of the Crop Photography Contest.  Winners in three different age categories will be awarded Bright Start college savings account scholarships ranging from $250 to $1,000.

The contest entry deadline is June 12th.  The competition, now in its 14th year, provides students ages 8 to 18 with a creative opportunity to share their vision of agriculture in our state.

“I enjoy hosting this contest each year because it inspires students to go out and explore the beauty of Illinois agriculture while also displaying their creative talents,” Frerichs said.  “Illinois is home to skilled and dedicated farmers, millions of acres of fertile farmland, and a diverse range of products, all of which make us a leader in the agricultural industry.”

The Treasurer’s Office is now accepting electronic submissions for the Cream of the Crop Photo Contest at this link. Each participating student may submit up to two photos by June 12th.

A panel of outside judges will choose the top photographs in three age-based categories: ages 8-10, 11-14 and 15-18.  Bright Start scholarships of $1,000, $500 and $250 will be awarded to students who place first, second or third in each of the three categories.

To read the rules, terms, and legal conditions associated with this contest, go to the Illinois State Treasurer’s Office website or contact Teri Whitfield at 217-900-0075.

Now in its 14th year, the photo contest offers Illinois students an opportunity to showcase their most innovative or scenic pictures that depict their vision of agriculture in our state.  Nearly 900 students have participated in the contest since it debuted in 2013, and they have submitted almost 1,600 photos.

The Cream of the Crop Photo Contest is part of the Illinois State Treasurer’s Ag Invest program.  Winning photos will be featured in Ag Invest marketing material and next year’s Cream of the Crop calendar, as well as at the 2026 Illinois State Fair.

Ag Invest is one of the nation’s largest agricultural linked deposit programs, celebrating 43 years in 2026.  It helps hundreds of Illinois farmers and agriculture professionals.  The Treasurer’s Office, through Ag Invest, partners with eligible financial institutions to offer farmers and ag businesses operating lines of credit and long-term, low-interest loans which can be used for operating costs, equipment purchases, construction-related expenses and livestock purchases.
